etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin appositus, past participle of adponere, from ad- + ponere (“to put, place”). See apposition.
senses: Strikingly appropriate or relevant; well suited to the circumstance or in relation to something.
Positioned at rest in respect to another, be it side-to-side, front-to-front, back-to-back, or even three-dimensionally: in apposition.
(rare) That which is apposite; something suitable.
